question:
A 52-year-old woman presents with fatigue and pain of the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints for the past 6 months. She also has knee and wrist pain that has been present for the past 2 months, with morning stiffness that improves over the course of the day. Physical examination is significant for subcutaneous nodules. Laboratory tests are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL
Red blood cell count 4.9 x 106/µL
White blood cell count 5,000/mm3
Platelet count 180,000/mm3
Coombs' test Negative
C-reactive peptide (CRP) Elevated
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) Negative
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP antibody) Moderately positive
Anti-nuclear antibody (ANA) Negative
Rheumatoid factor (RF) Negative
What is the most likely human leukocyte antigen (HLA) subtype associated with this disease?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Presence of subcutaneous nodules" -> "Possible rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Consider HLA subtype associated with rheumatoid arthritis" -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: "Moderately positive anti-CCP antibody" -> "Indicates rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Consider HLA subtype associated with rheumatoid arthritis" -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: "Negative rheumatoid factor (RF)" -> "Does not rule out rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Consider HLA subtype associated with rheumatoid arthritis" -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: "Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP)" -> "Indicates inflammation" -> "Consider HLA subtype associated with inflammatory conditions" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with subcutaneous nodules, moderately positive anti-CCP antibody, negative RF, and elevated CRP suggests a high likelihood of rheumatoid arthritis. Considering the HLA subtype associated with rheumatoid arthritis, the most likely option is HLA-DR4.
analysis: The patient's presentation with fatigue, joint pain, subcutaneous nodules, moderately positive anti-CCP antibody, negative RF, and elevated CRP is highly suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis. In rheumatoid arthritis, the most common HLA subtype associated is HLA-DR4.
